audit.why: 47.42% over 523 games with Lillia owning levels 3 and 4-5 and Rumble owning the first-item row matches the kit maths: Blooming Blows on 6/5.5/5/4.5/4s plus its stacking move speed out-paces a 600-range cone, and Liandry's is what finally burns through the kite. diff EVEN / 6/10 stands.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late spike named 'Lillia's Rift Bolts' — no such ability exists in her kit. Spike text also carried 'Watch Out Eep' and 'Her Lilting Lullaby ... Dream-Laden Bough' phrasing flagged by the packet.
audit.why: Her real abilities are Dream-Laden Bough (P), Blooming Blows (Q), Watch Out! Eep! (W), Swirlseed (E), Lilting Lullaby (R). 'Rift Bolts' is a fabrication a player would search for and not find.
audit.corrected: Replaced with Swirlseed and Dream-Laden Bough's max-health burn, and punctuated Watch Out! Eep! correctly. Attached real cooldowns: Q 6-4s, W 14-10s, E 12s flat, R 150/130/110s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three things. (a) Lilting Lullaby was written as a generic sleep-CC; it only affects enemies who already carry Dream-Laden Bough dust, which makes the counterplay pre-emptive, and that was never said. (b) Blooming Blows deals extra TRUE damage on its outer edge — the rim is the worst place to stand and no resistance helps there; absent from both layers. (c) 'your sleep-immune shield (W active) can eat one Lilting Lullaby DOT tick' is fabricated — Scrap Shield grants a shield and a move-speed burst, nothing about sleep immunity.
audit.why: Riot text — Lilting Lullaby: 'causes all enemies with Dream Dust on them to become Drowsy before falling asleep.' Blooming Blows: 'dealing extra true damage on the edge.' Scrap Shield: 'protecting him from damage and granting him a quick burst of speed.'
audit.corrected: Stated the dust prerequisite as the actual counterplay, stated the true-damage rim, and deleted the sleep-immunity claim.
sources: champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json (rumble vs lillia: resistances-invalidated on Blooming Blows)

audit.whatIsWrong: Range numbers were invented: 'your Flamespitter range is 500 units and her Blooming Blows bounce keeps her at 525+'. Also 'Double-cast Electro-Harpoon to cut her Lilting Lullaby escape path' treats her ultimate as an escape.
audit.why: Flamespitter is 600. Blooming Blows is 450, Watch Out! Eep! 500, Swirlseed 700. Lilting Lullaby is a 1600-range sleep, not mobility — Lillia has no dash anywhere in her kit, which is itself the useful fact: her only escape is stacked move speed, and a slow strips exactly that.
audit.corrected: Corrected all ranges and reframed the harpoons as move-speed strippers against a champion with no dash. Also documented Swirlseed continuing to roll until it hits a wall or a target, which is how it arrives from off-screen.

edits.before: Lillia is not a typical melee — she never walks straight into your Flamespitter. Her Blooming Blows bounces on you and the wave simultaneously, stacking her passive move speed without standing in your Q cone long enough to eat the damage. Level 1 is a wash: you can tick her with Q but she dances out before Danger Zone stacks. At Level 2 she starts stringing Blooming Blows into Watch Out! Eep! (W ground slam) to poke; if you step up to trade she has the speed to disengage before your double Electro-Harpoon lands both charges. Play the wave tight, keep your first Harpoon in reserve, and do not chase her through the jungle or you will Overheat in the open with no shield.
edits.after: Lillia never walks into your Flamespitter — Blooming Blows is a 450-range burst around her on a 6-second cooldown, and every spell hit stacks her move speed, so she taps you and the wave and drifts back out. Level 1 is a wash: you can tick her at the tip of your 600 cone but she leaves before Danger Zone matters. From 2 she strings Blooming Blows into Watch Out! Eep! (500 range, heaviest in the centre) and pokes. Watch the edge of her Q — that outer rim deals true damage, so armour and MR do nothing there; be inside it or fully outside it, never on the rim. Hold one Electro Harpoon in reserve for the moment she commits, and never chase her into the jungle: you will Overheat in the open with nothing to cast.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 she cements her kite pattern and the lane belongs to her — your Flamespitter range is 500 units and her Blooming Blows bounce keeps her at 525+. The moment you enter Danger Zone she respects the threat and backs off; if you burn Heat trying to chase, you Overheat and she walks back in for free autos. Your play is patience: freeze the wave on your side so she must overextend to last-hit, then punish that one step too far with double Electro-Harpoon into Danger Zone Q. At Level 6 the math shifts slightly — Equalizer laid across the bush line or river denies her flanks and your sleep-immune shield (W active) can eat one Lilting Lullaby DOT tick, but you are not favoured here. The spike to watch: if she hits 6 and you have no ultimate, she can sleep-combo you into a genuine all-in threat.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 she cements the kite and the lane is hers. Flamespitter reaches 600 units and burns for 3 seconds, but Blooming Blows refreshes every 4.5-5 seconds by then and each hit adds move speed, so she is always one step past your cone. Enter Danger Zone and she simply leaves; chase and you Overheat, which locks you out of casting entirely while she walks back in for free autos. Play patience: freeze on your side so she must overextend to last-hit, then punish that one step with both Electro Harpoons for the magic-resist shred into a Danger Zone Flamespitter. At 6, Lilting Lullaby (150s) only puts to sleep enemies already carrying Dream-Laden Bough dust — so the counterplay starts before she ults: refuse the chip that marks you, because Scrap Shield does nothing against sleep. Lay The Equalizer across the bush line to deny her flank.

edits.before: Liandry's Torment turns the page — your sustained Flamespitter now burns her through the kite, and the item's DOT stacks while she spends her Blooming Blows window. Force her into choke-points where Equalizer denies her escape arc, because she cannot kite you through a rocket wall. In teamfights, drop Equalizer across the path she uses to cycle Blooming Blows on your carries; she must either eat the slow-and-burn or lose her damage window entirely. If she reaches Rabadon's before you snowball the lead, her passive DOT and Lullaby teamfight become a genuine problem — close the game through Equalizer impact, not 1v1 duels, where she retains the kite advantage at full build.
edits.after: Liandry's Torment turns the page — your Flamespitter now burns her through the kite and the item stacks while she spends her Blooming Blows window. Force her into choke-points: she has no dash anywhere in her kit, so her only escape is stacked move speed and The Equalizer's slow strips exactly that. In teamfights lay it across the path she uses to cycle Blooming Blows onto your carries; she either eats the burn or loses her damage window. Watch Swirlseed (12s, 700 range) — if it hits nothing it keeps rolling until it meets a wall or a target, so it arrives from off-screen down a lane. Close the game through Equalizer impact, not duels, where her kite holds at full build.

notes: Fabrication removed: "Lillia's Rift Bolts" (content.spikes[3].text) is not an ability she has — replaced with Swirlseed and Dream-Laden Bough. Second fabrication removed: "your sleep-immune shield (W active) can eat one Lilting Lullaby DOT tick" — Scrap Shield has no sleep interaction in Riot's text, so the page now says plainly that it does not stop sleep. Invented ranges corrected: Flamespitter is 600 (page said 500) and Blooming Blows is 450 (page said she "keeps her at 525+"). Lilting Lullaby was treated as an escape tool in wants.you[1]; it is a 1600-range sleep, and the genuinely useful fact is that Lillia has NO dash in her kit, so a slow is a hard counter to her disengage. Pronouns: the full layer called Lillia "he"/"him" in winCon, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.mid and report[1]; fixed in every string I touched. UNVERIFIED, left alone: report[8].t recommends Mercury's Treads. Whether tenacity shortens Lilting Lullaby's Drowsy/sleep is not in Riot's description and I did not verify it, so I did not add or remove that reasoning. Rumble kit-flag misfires (Scrap Shield "knockup"/"terrain", The Equalizer "terrain") are not asserted anywhere here; note that _missing-interactions.json tells Lillia's own page that Rumble "can cut your retreat" with them, which is wrong for Scrap Shield.
